title: 2021年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2021年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 With obesity now affecting 29% of the population in England, and expected to rise to 35% by 2030, should we now recognise it as a disease? Obesity, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that health may be adversely affected, meets the dictionary definition of disease, argues Professor John Wilding. He points out that more than 200 genes influence weight. "Thus body weight is strongly influenced by biology—it is not an individual's fault if they develop obesity." Yet the widespread view is that obesity is self-induced and that it is entirely the individual's responsibility to do something about it. Recognising obesity as a chronic disease with severe complications rather than a lifestyle choice "should help reduce the stigma(耻辱) and discrimination experienced by many people with obesity," he adds.

P2 Professor Wilding disagrees that labelling a high proportion of the population as having a disease removes personal responsibility or may overwhelm health services, pointing out that other common diseases, such as high blood pressure and diabetes, require people to take action to manage their condition. He suggests that most people with obesity will eventually develop complications. "But unless we accept that obesity is a disease, we are not going to be able to tackle it," he concludes.

P3 But Dr. Richard Pile, a physician with a special interest in diabetes, argues that adopting this approach "could actually result in worse outcomes for individuals and society." He believes that the dictionary definition of disease "is so vague that we can classify almost anything as a disease" and says the question is not whether we can, but whether we should, and to what end.

P4 If labelling obesity as a disease was harmless then it wouldn't really matter, he writes. But labelling obesity as a disease "risks reducing autonomy, disempowering and robbing people of the intrinsic(内在的) motivation that is such an important enabler of change." What's more, making obesity a disease "may not benefit patients, but it will benefit healthcare providers and the pharmaceutical(制药的) industry when health insurance and clinical guidelines promote treatment with drugs and surgery," he warns.

questions.q: What does Professor John Wilding argue about obesity?
options: Its impact on society is expected to rise.
It is now too widespread to be neglected.
It should be regarded as a genetic disease.
Its dictionary definition should be updated.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Professor John Wilding argue about obesity? 问的是这位教授关于肥胖的** 主张**，答案要在原文的明确表述中找，不需要跨段综合，是典型的细节题。

【拆句】题干 What does Professor John Wilding argue about obesity? 是标准的 what + 主语 + 动词 + 介词短语 结构，主语「Professor John Wilding」，谓语「argue」，「about obesity」是 argue 的话题状语；句子平铺直叙，无陷阱。 46. What does Professor John Wilding argue about obesity? A) Its impact on society is expected to rise. B) It is now too widespread to be neglected. C) It should be regarded as a genetic disease. D) Its dictionary definition should be updated.

【定位】He points out that more than 200 genes influence weight. "Thus body weight is strongly influenced by biology—it is not an individual's fault if they develop obesity." 他指出有超过 200 个基因影响体重。「因此体重受生物学因素强烈影响——一个人如果得 了肥胖症，并不是他自己的过错。」

【选项】A) 张冠李戴：把背景数据安到具名人物头上 Its impact on society is expected to rise. 实际上是文章开头那句 obesity now affecting 29% of the population in England, and expected to rise to 35% by 2030 的概括，是作者交代的背景数据，并非 Wilding 教授「argue about obesity」的 主张。 B) 无中生有：常识合理但原文未支撑 It is now too widespread to be neglected. 是个看似合理的概括，但 Wilding 全文论 证的是「肥胖应被视为疾病」「不是个人过错」，从未以「太普遍以至于无法忽视」为 论点；原文虽提到 29%/35% 的数据，但落点是「该不该承认为疾病」，与「too widespread to be neglected」不构成等值。 C) ✓ 正确 more than 200 genes influence weight ↔a genetic disease not an individual's fault if they develop obesity ↔regarded as a genetic disease 预判抓住「肥胖与基因强相关 + 应作为疾病看待」两个要点，It should be regarded as a genetic disease. 恰好同时覆盖这两点，与 Wilding 在 P1 的主张完全对齐。 D) 偷换概念：动词替换改变命题 Its dictionary definition should be updated. 偷换了原文的「meets the dictionary definition」——Wilding 是说「肥胖**符合**字典关于 disease 的定义」，主张承认它 **是**疾病，不是主张**更新**字典定义；选项把「符合定义」偷换成「更新定义」。 大众对肥胖症的看法是什么? A) 它难以定义。 B) 它是一种现代疾病。 C) 它与基因有很大关系。 D) 它源于缺乏自我控制。

questions.q: What is the popular view of obesity?
options: It is difficult to define.
It is a modern disease.
It has much to do with one's genes.
It results from a lack of self-control.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the popular view of obesity? 问的是「大众对肥胖的看法是什么」，要找的是原 文中对大众观点的客观陈述，属于细节题。

【拆句】题干 What is the popular view of obesity? 是简单的 what is + 名词短语 结构，「of obesity」是 popular view 的修饰，限定看法的对象；结构简单，无陷阱。 47. What is the popular view of obesity? A) It is difficult to define. B) It is a modern disease. C) It has much to do with one's genes. D) It results from a lack of self-control.

【定位】Yet the widespread view is that obesity is self-induced and that it is entirely the individual's responsibility to do something about it. 然而，普遍的观点认为，肥胖是自找的，并且完全是个人自己的责任去采取行动加以解决。

【选项】A) 无中生有：抓住选项与原文方向相反的反例 It is difficult to define. 关于「肥胖难以定义」的说法在原文找不到任何依据；原文 P1 明确给出了肥胖的定义（excess body fat …），反而是「易定义」的方向，与本选项 相反。 B) 答非所问：与题干所问对象不对齐 It is a modern disease. 想说「肥胖是一种现代疾病」，但原文 the widespread view 描述的大众观点是「自找的、个人责任」，从未把大众观点概括为「现代疾病」；而且 大众观点恰恰是「不视为疾病」，与「modern disease」方向冲突。 C) 张冠李戴：用对立方观点冒充本方观点 It has much to do with one's genes. 实际上是 Wilding 教授的主张（more than 200 genes influence weight），而非大众观点；原文用 Yet 把大众观点与 Wilding 主张明 确切开——大众恰好是不认基因这一论的。 D) ✓ 正确 obesity is self-induced ↔results from a lack of self-control it is entirely the individual's responsibility to do something about it ↔a lack of self-control 预判要点「自找的 + 自己负责」分别对应到 results from a lack of self-control 中的 「self-control」与「lack of」，D 是唯一同时覆盖这两点的选项。 为什么有些人反对将肥胖症归类为疾病? A) 肥胖者将不会感到有责任采取任何行动。 B) 肥胖者将无力承担医疗费用。 C) 肥胖者将被焦虑所淹没。 D) 肥胖者将受到歧视。

questions.q: Why are some people opposed to labelling obesity as a disease?
options: Obese people would not feel responsible to take any action.
Obese people would not be able to afford the medical costs.
Obese people would be overwhelmed with anxiety.
Obese people would be discriminated against.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why are some people opposed to labelling obesity as a disease? 问的是反方反对的具 体原因，对应原文反方论据的明确陈述，属于细节题。

【拆句】题干 Why are some people opposed to labelling obesity as a disease? 主干是 why + be + 主语 + 过去分词作表语 (opposed to)，labelling … as a disease 是动名词短语作 to 的宾语；结构稍长但平铺直叙，无陷阱。 48. Why are some people opposed to labelling obesity as a disease? A) Obese people would not feel responsible to take any action. B) Obese people would not be able to afford the medical costs. C) Obese people would be overwhelmed with anxiety. D) Obese people would be discriminated against.

【定位】But labelling obesity as a disease "risks reducing autonomy, disempowering and robbing people of the intrinsic motivation that is such an important enabler of change." 但把肥胖定性为疾病「有可能削弱人的自主性，让人失去权能感，并夺走对改变如此重要的 内在动力。」

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 reducing autonomy, disempowering and robbing people of the intrinsic motivation ↔ not feel responsible to take any action other common diseases, such as high blood pressure and diabetes, require people to take action to manage their condition ↔to take any action 预判要点「失去自主与改变动力」在四个选项里只有 Obese people would not feel responsible to take any action. 能落地——「失去内在动力 + 失去自主」≈「不觉得 自己有责任行动」。 B) 无中生有：把次相关话题拉来当依据 Obese people would not be able to afford the medical costs. 关于「肥胖者支付不 起医疗费用」在原文找不到任何对应；原文末段提到的费用相关内容是 health insurance and clinical guidelines promote treatment with drugs and surgery，谈 的是谁受益（机构与药企），不是谁付不起。 C) 偷换概念：把动力问题偷换为情绪问题 Obese people would be overwhelmed with anxiety. 把原文「失去 intrinsic motivation」（失去改变的内在动力）偷换为「被焦虑压垮」（情绪问题）——前者关 乎主体动力是否减弱，后者关乎情绪是否上升，方向不一致。 D) 张冠李戴：把正方支持理由当反方反对理由 Obese people would be discriminated against. 实际上是 Wilding 在 should help reduce the stigma and discrimination experienced by many people with obesity 提到的——把肥胖视为疾病可以**减少**歧视，是 Wilding 支持贴标签的理由；本题问 的是**反对**贴标签的理由，正反阵营完全相反。 Richard Pile 博士如何看待词典中关于疾病的定义? A) 它对理解肥胖症毫无用处。 B) 它过于宽泛因而缺乏明确性。 C) 它对解决患者的问题帮助甚微。 D) 它对关于肥胖症的争论影响甚微。

questions.q: What does Dr. Richard Pile think of the dictionary definition of disease?
options: It is of no use in understanding obesity.
It is too inclusive and thus lacks clarity.
It helps little to solve patients' problems.
It matters little to the debate over obesity.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Dr. Richard Pile think of the dictionary definition of disease? 问的是具名人 物对一个具体概念的看法，原文中有他直接的评价句，属于细节题。

【拆句】题干 What does Dr. Richard Pile think of the dictionary definition of disease? 主干是 what + do/does + 主语 + think of + 宾语，think of 是固定搭配「对……的看法」；结构 常规，无陷阱。

【定位】He believes that the dictionary definition of disease "is so vague that we can classify almost anything as a disease" and says the question is not whether we can, but whether we should, and to what end. 他认为，对 disease 一词的字典定义「过于含糊，以至于我们几乎可以把任何东西都归入疾 病」，并说问题不在于「我们能不能」，而在于「我们该不该，以及目的何在」。

【选项】A) 过度推断：把局部批评放大成全盘否定 It is of no use in understanding obesity. 把 Pile 的「定义含糊」推得过远——他只 是说定义太宽泛而已，没说「字典定义对理解肥胖毫无用处」；恰恰相反，他的论证起 点正是「按字典定义看，肥胖确实可被归入 disease」（the question is not whether we can）。 B) ✓ 正确 is so vague that we can classify almost anything as a disease ↔ too inclusive and thus lacks clarity is so vague that we can classify almost anything as a disease ↔and thus 预判要点「过于含糊 + 范围过广」在选项里精准对位为 too inclusive and thus lacks clarity，是唯一覆盖两个语义点的选项。 C) 答非所问：偷偷把问域换到下一步 It helps little to solve patients' problems. 谈的是「字典定义对解决患者问题帮助不 大」，把焦点从「定义本身的特性」偏移到「定义对患者的影响」；题干 What does Dr. Richard Pile think of the dictionary definition of disease? 问的是 Pile 对**定义 本身**的看法。 D) 与原文相反：极性反转 It matters little to the debate over obesity. 说「字典定义对肥胖之争没什么关系」， 但 Pile 在 P3 整段都在围绕字典定义展开批评，并以此为立论起点（the dictionary definition of disease is so vague）；可见字典定义对他**至关重要**，与「matters little」语义相反。 Richard Pile 博士对将肥胖症归类为疾病有何担忧? A) 它可能影响肥胖者的生活质量。 B) 它可能加速肥胖症的蔓延。 C) 它可能导致医生短缺。 D) 它可能对患者没什么好处。

questions.q: What is Dr. Richard Pile's concern about classifying obesity as a disease?
options: It may affect obese people's quality of life.
It may accelerate the spread of obesity.
It may cause a shortage of doctors.
It may do little good to patients.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is Dr. Richard Pile's concern about classifying obesity as a disease? 问的是 Pile 担忧的具体内容，原文末段有明确陈述，属于细节题。

【拆句】题干 What is Dr. Richard Pile's concern about classifying obesity as a disease? 主干是 what + be + 主语，「about classifying obesity as a disease」是 concern 的修饰短 语，限定担忧的对象；结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】What's more, making obesity a disease "may not benefit patients, but it will benefit healthcare providers and the pharmaceutical industry when health insurance and clinical guidelines promote treatment with drugs and surgery," he warns. 此外，他警告说，把肥胖变成一种疾病「未必使患者受益，但当医保和临床指南推动用药物 和手术进行治疗时，它将让医疗机构和制药业受益」。 50. What is Dr. Richard Pile's concern about classifying obesity as a disease? A) It may affect obese people's quality of life. B) It may accelerate the spread of obesity. C) It may cause a shortage of doctors. D) It may do little good to patients.

【选项】A) 无中生有：用合理却未现的概念顶替 It may affect obese people's quality of life. 关于「影响肥胖者生活质量」在原文找不 到对应表述；Pile 的担忧落在「医疗效用」和「自主与动力」上，不是「生活质量」这 个独立维度。 B) 与原文相反/混搭：把背景趋势伪装成反方担忧 It may accelerate the spread of obesity. 说贴疾病标签会「加速肥胖蔓延」，但原文 Pile 担忧的是「会让人失去改变动力」（robbing people of the intrinsic motivation）——这是「不利于改善」的间接后果，但与「加速蔓延」是两码事；而且 P1 中肥胖的扩张趋势是 Wilding 立场的背景数据，与 Pile 的担忧无关。 C) 无中生有：用相邻话题词凭空造命题 It may cause a shortage of doctors. 关于「导致医生短缺」在原文找不到任何依据； 原文末段提到 healthcare providers and the pharmaceutical industry 会受益，恰恰 是「医疗供给方得利」的方向，与「短缺」相反。 D) ✓ 正确 may not benefit patients ↔may do little good to patients may not benefit patients, but it will benefit healthcare providers and the pharmaceutical industry ↔do little good to patients 四个选项里只有 It may do little good to patients. 在主体（患者）与极性（益处不 大）两端都与 Pile 的核心担忧一致；其余选项要么换了担忧对象，要么改了担忧内容。
